question: Is the Chinese bank account recorded under your foreign passport or under a Chinese ID?
why_it_decides: This one fact picks which half of the rule book applies. A passport account is a 境外个人 account; a Chinese-ID account is a 境内个人 account, and the two have different quota and document rules.
known: The PBOC Measures classify by the ID document produced when the account was opened (Art. 37). The State Council Regulation, Art. 52, separately calls a foreigner who has lived in China for one continuous year a 境内个人. The two definitions do not line up.
unknown: Which definition the bank actually applied to this account.
how_to_discover: Ask the branch in writing for the account subject category (账户主体类别) and keep the reply. Free of charge: 95566 or any branch counter.

question: How long have you lived in China in the current or last tax year; are you a Chinese tax resident?
why_it_decides: Residence decides whether China taxes your worldwide income or only China-source income, and whether you are a 居民个人 for the 3%-45% scale.
known: Individual Income Tax Law Art. 1: resident if domiciled in China or present 183 days in a tax year; residents pay on worldwide income, non-residents on China-source income.
unknown: Your actual day count and domicile position.
how_to_discover: Count days from entry stamps and your residence permit; confirm with the local tax office (12366).

question: What is the money, line by line: salary, business profit, a home sale, rent, a gift, an inheritance, or money you brought in from abroad?
why_it_decides: The bank's document list, the Chinese tax treatment and the available route all hang off this, not off the amount.
known: Art. 59 requires source-of-funds material including tax evidence for income earned in China; Art. 65 needs only ID for FX already in the account; the 2004 announcement covers only pre-departure property and inheritances.
how_to_discover: Sort the bank statements by counterparty for the last 3-5 years and label every deposit. This is the single most useful document you can produce for the bank.

question: Has Chinese individual income tax already been paid or withheld on the money that is in the account?
why_it_decides: If it has, the bank's tax evidence is a formality. If it has not, the tax is owed whether or not the money ever leaves China, and no channel removes it.
known: Art. 3: 3%-45% on wages and service income, 20% flat on dividends, interest, rent, property gains and incidental income. Savings-deposit interest accrued from 2008-10-09 is exempt.
unknown: Whether the payer withheld, and whether you have the certificates.
how_to_discover: Pull a 完税证明 (tax payment certificate) for the last five years from the local tax office or the 个人所得税 app. It shows what was withheld, by whom, and when.

question: Is any part of the balance a gift, or money whose origin you cannot document?
why_it_decides: No lawful route was found for RMB received as a gift inside China by a passport holder, or for RMB with no traceable origin. This is the one case with no verified channel.
known: Art. 59 requires source material. SAFE's answers describe income and property, not gifts. The Regulation lets the bank refuse a transaction whose authenticity it doubts (Art. 68 of the 2020 guidelines).
unknown: Whether a gift is involved and, if so, the donor's own documents.
how_to_discover: Ask the branch in writing before converting anything. In parallel, the person who gave the money may be able to remit it themselves under one of the documented routes.

question: What exactly did the bank say would be charged: a tax, a fee, a spread, or a refusal to convert? Which office said it, and in writing?
why_it_decides: The brief says 'a considerable amount of taxes'. No official source read for this release imposes a tax on converting or wiring. If the number is a spread or a fee, it is negotiable and much smaller than a tax. If it is unpaid income tax, it is not a conversion penalty at all.
known: State Council Regulation Art. 5: no restriction on current international payments and transfers. No tax on the conversion itself was found in any source read.
unknown: The actual words used, the rate, the amount, and who said them.
how_to_discover: Ask for the quote in writing with the tariff item or legal basis named. If a tax is asserted, ask for the assessment document (完税凭证 / 税务事项通知书).

question: Does the branch actually operate the route you qualify for, and at what rate and fee?
why_it_decides: All cost figures here are Bank of China's published board and its standard personal tariff. The tariff itself allows agreed, promotional and local variations.
known: S02 note 1: 另有协议约定、价格优惠、地方性收费差异的，按照协议或当地公示的内容收取相关费用.
unknown: This branch's executable rate, its fee, and whether it will run a large personal remittance at all.
how_to_discover: Get a dated written quote for the whole amount, including the correspondent and receiving bank. Compare at least two banks.

question: When and at what rate did you acquire the RMB? Do you have the records?
why_it_decides: The U.S. currency gain depends entirely on your cost basis in the RMB. On USD 400,000 the spread between a 2024 and a 2025 acquisition is hundreds of dollars of gain and, at the top rate, hundreds of dollars of tax.
known: §988(c)(1)(C): disposing of non-functional currency is a §988 transaction. IRS publishes yearly average rates (2024: 7.189, 2025: 7.129 CNY/USD).
how_to_discover: Reconstruct from bank statements and payslips by year, and use the IRS yearly average for each year, consistently.

question: Is moving this balance a 'personal transaction' for §988(e) purposes, and is any gain in the realistic range below USD 200?
why_it_decides: §988(e) relief only applies up to USD 200 of gain. Above that the whole gain is ordinary income, so for any balance of the size described here the relief does not apply.
known: §988(e)(2) text: the exclusion does not apply if the gain would exceed $200.
unknown: Your marginal rate this year, which sets the tax on the gain.
how_to_discover: Run the figure with your tax preparer before you convert, not after.

question: Have you filed FBARs and Form 8938 for every year the account existed?
why_it_decides: A missed report is a separate exposure from any tax and is larger than every bank fee in this release combined: USD 16,536 non-willful per report, or the greater of USD 165,353 or 50% of the balance if willful.
known: FBAR threshold USD 10,000 aggregate at any time in the calendar year; Form 8938 thresholds USD 50,000/75,000 for an unmarried filer living in the US, with a USD 60,000 penalty ceiling.
unknown: Whether the account was ever reported, and for which years.
how_to_discover: Check your filed returns and the BSA E-Filing system. If anything is missing, get advice before you move the money: the move does not create the obligation, but it makes the account visible.

question: Were you ever a mainland resident with a Chinese hukou that has since been cancelled?
why_it_decides: If yes, the emigrant property transfer (L06) is the only route with no annual amount ceiling and no need to fit the money into a current-income category. If no, it is unavailable and the answer changes completely.
known: The 2004 announcement covers 移民 (emigrants) and 继承人 (heirs) only; approval is at the former hukou.
unknown: Your hukou history and whether you hold the cancellation certificate (户籍注销证明).
how_to_discover: The police station that held your hukou issues the cancellation certificate; the embassy or consulate certifies your settlement abroad.

question: Do you hold the PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card (not a visa, not a residence permit)?
why_it_decides: It is the only way a foreign passport holder gets the USD 50,000 a year convenience amount. Without it, every conversion needs documents.
known: Art. 59 second sentence: 持有外国人永久居留身份证的境外个人适用购汇年度便利化额度.
how_to_discover: Check the card; the number is printed on it.

question: Is any part of the balance already in a foreign-currency account inside China?
why_it_decides: Foreign currency already in the account can be wired out on ID alone with no conversion and no spread: the cheapest lawful route in this release.
known: Art. 65(1): 外汇账户内外汇汇出，凭本人有效身份证件办理.
unknown: The currency split of the balance.
how_to_discover: Look at the account statement: USD and CNY sub-accounts are listed separately.

question: Do you need the whole amount at once, or can it move over several years?
why_it_decides: The quota route takes eight calendar years for USD 400,000 and the ATM route about 27. Everything else is limited by approval time, not by annual amounts.
known: USD 50,000 a year per person on the PR-ID card; RMB 100,000 a year per person on overseas ATM withdrawals.
how_to_discover: Decide the cash need first; it eliminates routes faster than the cost tables do.

question: Will the money move in one wire or several, and who pays the correspondent bank fee (OUR/SHA/BEN)?
why_it_decides: The wire tariff is capped at RMB 260 plus RMB 150, so splitting adds fees almost linearly, while the exchange spread is proportional and unchanged. The charge code decides who absorbs the correspondent fee.
known: BOC tariff: 0.1%, min RMB 50, max RMB 260, plus RMB 150 cable.
unknown: The receiving bank's incoming-wire fee and its charge code policy.
how_to_discover: Ask your US bank for its incoming international wire fee schedule in writing.

gate: Gate 7 — the rest of the world
question: Is the balance below the reporting thresholds, so that none of the U.S. reporting penalties can bite?
why_it_decides: Below USD 10,000 aggregate the FBAR question disappears; below USD 50,000/75,000 so does Form 8938 for a single filer in the US. Above them, the reporting is not optional.
unknown: Peak balance in the account in each calendar year.
how_to_discover: Pull the year-end and peak statements for every year the account was open.

gate: Gate 7 — the rest of the world
question: Are you a US citizen by birth or naturalisation, and do you hold any other passport?
why_it_decides: US citizenship drives the worldwide reporting. A second passport may open a receiving account in another currency, which changes the conversion leg but not the US tax on the gain.
known: §988 applies to a US person wherever the conversion happens.
how_to_discover: No discovery needed; this is a fact you hold.
